title: real published SBC examples (rounded)
input_audit_method: Source-page review of the nine coverage examples in the three locally supplied SBCs. Numeric episode costs transcribed from Total Example Cost; these are not service-level allowed prices.
rounding_note: Analyst-selected conservative $200 absolute total envelope: four published components, each rounded by at most $50. CMS instructions p. 4 round costs above $100 to $100 and below $100 to $10, with OOP-cap adjustment. This envelope alone cannot establish component accuracy or exact adjudication. No predictions were available to apply it to in this run.
methodology: Official rounded illustrations, not actual adjudicated claims, bills, or savings measurements.
All 18 published labels retained; compilation attempted for nine examples across three insurers; other nine explicitly not attempted.
Compiler failures and missing scenario inputs block calculation; no manual gold policy, invented CPT codes, inferred service counts or episode-price substitution.
Published component addition checks transcription only; it is never counted as independent patient-cost recalculation.

Nine SBC example pages were reviewed for input sufficiency: published episode costs are available, but service quantities and per-service allowed prices are absent. Patient cost-sharing outputs are excluded from prediction inputs.
Kaiser EOC compilation is reported separately; no merger with the SBC was attempted.
Accuracy and mean absolute error are null when no scenario can be independently recalculated.
SYNTHETIC_kaiser_demo_replay.json and all bundled synthetic benchmarks are excluded.

Out-of-network coverage is generally not provided; only emergency room, emergency medical transportation, and urgent care when temporarily outside service area are covered out-of-network. No out-of-network deductible or OOP max is defined.
Mail order pharmacy benefits are omitted because they are per-prescription charges not directly comparable to retail copays and have supply limits; the engine handles simple retail copays.
Specialty drugs (Tier 4) have 20% coinsurance up to $250 per prescription; the cap cannot be represented by the simple coinsurance model, so benefit is omitted.
Facility fee for hospital stay ($375/day up to 5 days) is per-day cap, which is not representable; omitted.
Inpatient mental health has $375/day up to 5 days; per-day cap omitted.
Rehabilitation services inpatient $375/day up to 5 days; per-day cap omitted.
Habilitation services inpatient $375/day up to 5 days; per-day cap omitted.
Skilled nursing care is $150/day up to 5 days; per-day cap omitted.
Outpatient services for mental health: other outpatient services no charge; group mental health $20, group substance abuse $5; these variants omitted as not simple individual visit.
Maternity office visits no charge and childbirth/delivery professional services not applicable; facility services $375/day up to 5 days; per-day cap omitted.
Children's eye exam, glasses, dental check-up no charge; but these are age-limited and require additional information; omitted.

Out-of-network benefits: all out-of-network services are listed as 'Not covered' in the SBC, except emergency room and urgent care which have copayments. However, no out-of-network deductible or OOP maximum is provided; therefore, an out-of-network network object is omitted.

Balance billing: The document mentions balance-billed charges are not included in the OOP limit, but does not explicitly state whether the plan protects against balance billing for in-network or out-of-network providers. Therefore, balance_billing is set to null for both networks.
Family-level deductible and OOP maximum: Only individual amounts are compiled; family amounts are not included in this extraction because the engine supports individual pools.

Omitted benefits with per-day or multi-day limits: Tier 2 and Tier 3 prescription drug copays vary by supply (e.g., $30/$60/$90) and are not compilable into a single numeric copay without an engine-supported supply condition. They are omitted.
Tier 4 prescription drugs use coinsurance with minimum and maximum dollar amounts, which the engine cannot represent.

Outpatient surgery, hospital stay, mental health services, pregnancy, home health care, rehabilitation, habilitation, skilled nursing, durable medical equipment, hospice, and children's dental/eye care are omitted due to copayments or coinsurance that are not simple fixed amounts or due to limitations/conditions that require additional claim context or exceed engine capabilities.
Some services have precertification requirements; these are not modeled as conditions because they are administrative requirements, not benefit-eligibility facts.

The emergency medical transportation benefit is a 30% coinsurance with no copay, but because it applies to both in- and out-of-network with no deductible and no OOP accumulation, it is omitted due to the lack of an out-of-network pool and potential balance billing issues.

Omitted benefit rows with per-day or multi-day caps: Hospital facility fee ($375 copay/day for max 5 days), Inpatient mental health services ($375 copay/day for max 5 days), Childbirth/delivery facility services ($375 copay/day for max 5 days), Skilled nursing center ($150 copay/day for max 5 days) because the engine cannot represent per-day caps.

Omitted prescription drug mail order variants and specialty drugs because retail is the common simple variant; mail order copays ($36 generic, $120 preferred brand, $170 non-preferred brand) and specialty drugs (20% coinsurance up to $250 per prescription) require calculation order not supported.

Omitted outpatient surgery facility fee non-hospital/ASC variant: 20% coinsurance for services other than surgery because coinsurance-only variant requires no mixed copay/coinsurance ordering assumption but is not a simple flat copay.
Omitted emergency room professional services (no charge) as a separate benefit because it is part of the ER row but can be captured as a condition in a future enhancement.
Omitted mental health outpatient services other than office visit (no charge) and inpatient services due to per-day cap.
Omitted preventive care cost-sharing for non-preventive services as a condition because the source states 'You may have to pay for services that aren't preventive' but does not specify the cost.
